declaration.preface:
PennEngineering & Manufacturing Corp. (“PennEngineering”) (Group) is an international manufacturer specializing in advanced fastening solutions and installation technologies used across sectors including automotive, electronics, industrial machinery, and telecommunications. Through continuous innovation, engineering excellence, and high-precision manufacturing processes, the Company provides reliable fastening systems that enhance product performance and support efficient assembly for customers across global markets.

PennEngineering believes that respect for human rights and responsible labor practices are fundamental to ethical business conduct and long-term sustainability. The Company is committed to maintaining a workplace where all individuals are treated with dignity, fairness, and respect. This commitment includes promoting equal opportunities, ensuring safe and healthy working conditions, prohibiting any form of forced or child labor, preventing discrimination and harassment, and supporting fair wages and working hours in line with applicable laws and recognized labor standards. Through these commitments, PennEngineering aims to foster a responsible and inclusive work environment across its operations and business relationships.
declaration.declaration: PennEngineering is committed to respecting human rights and promoting responsible labor practices across its global operations. The Company strives to provide a safe, fair, and inclusive workplace where employees are treated with dignity and respect. PennEngineering integrates labor and human rights considerations into its business practices and works to ensure that its operations comply with applicable labor laws and internationally recognized human rights standards.
declaration.scope:
This Responsible Labor and Human Rights Roadmap applies to all PennEngineering operations, including manufacturing facilities, engineering centers, offices, and distribution activities globally. The Roadmap applies to all employees, Workers, contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders involved in the Company’s operations and value chain.

PennEngineering operates in multiple countries with different business operations and regulatory requirements related to labor and human rights. While this roadmap’s vision and objectives apply across all locations, each facility will implement these principles in accordance with local regulations, operational requirements, and internal best practices

focusAreas: Prevention of Child Labor, Forced Labor, and Human Trafficking

Employee Health and Safety: PennEngineering prioritizes the health and safety of its employees by maintaining safe working conditions and implementing effective occupational health and safety management practices. The Company works to identify workplace hazards, reduce risks, and prevent work-related injuries and illnesses. Safety training, monitoring systems, and preventive programs are implemented to ensure a safe and healthy working environment across all facilities.
Career Management and Training: PennEngineering supports employee development by providing opportunities for continuous learning, skill enhancement, and professional growth. Training programs are designed to improve employee competencies, enhance workplace performance, and support long-term career development.
Working Conditions: PennEngineering is committed to maintaining fair working conditions in accordance with applicable labor laws and regulations. The Company promotes fair wages, reasonable working hours, and workplace practices that support employee well-being and work-life balance.
Social Dialogue and Employee Engagement: PennEngineering values open communication and constructive dialogue between employees and management. The Company encourages employees to share feedback, raise concerns, and participate in workplace discussions through established communication channels. Where applicable, the Company respects employees’ rights to freedom of association and collective representation.
Prevention of Child Labor, Forced Labor,: PennEngineering strictly prohibits the use of child labor, forced labor, bonded labor, or any form of human trafficking within its operations and supply chain. The Company ensures compliance with minimum employment age requirements and promotes ethical labor practices across its business relationships.
Prevention of Discrimination and Harassm: PennEngineering promotes a workplace free from discrimination, harassment, and intimidation. The Company supports equal employment opportunities and fair treatment regardless of gender, race, nationality, religion, disability, or other personal characteristics.

policy.monitoring:
PennEngineering is committed to regularly monitoring labor practices and human rights performance across its operations and reporting progress toward its labor and human rights objectives and targets. Key performance indicators such as workplace safety performance, employee training participation, employee engagement levels, grievance reporting, diversity metrics, and compliance with labor standards are monitored across operational facilities.

The Human Resources (HR) and Site Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) teams, in coordination with operational management, are responsible for collecting and reviewing workforce-related performance data. This information is used to evaluate progress toward labor and human rights goals, identify improvement opportunities, and ensure compliance with applicable labor laws and company policies.

PennEngineering periodically reviews workforce and human rights performance through internal management reviews, employee engagement feedback mechanisms, and compliance assessments. Relevant workforce and human rights information may also be shared through sustainability reports, customer sustainability assessments, or other external reporting frameworks where appropriate.

Through consistent monitoring, transparent communication, and continuous improvement initiatives, PennEngineering aims to strengthen accountability and uphold responsible labor practices and respect for human rights across its global operations.
policy.reviewMechanism:
The Human Resources (HR) leadership, shall be responsible for conducting the annual review of this Responsible Labor and Human Rights Roadmap. The review will assess the Roadmap effectiveness, progress toward labor and human rights targets, and compliance with applicable labor laws, regulations, and internationally recognized human rights standards.

Any updates or revisions resulting from organizational changes, regulatory developments, or stakeholder feedback will be incorporated into the Roadmap and communicated across relevant operational sites. This process ensures that the Roadmap remains aligned with PennEngineering’s commitment to responsible labor practices, employee well-being, and respect for human rights across its operations.
